questiontext.text:
A statement like the one in the exercise above: if \(p\) is a prime number with \({@lo@} \lt p \lt {@hi@}\), then \((p - 1)(p + 1)\) is a multiple of 12.

A proof by exhaustion checks one case for each such prime. Enter the set of these primes. Type a set in curly brackets, for example {5, 6}.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

generalfeedback.text:
The hypothesis says exactly which numbers are cases: primes, strictly between {@lo@} and {@hi@}. So the cases are {@ta1@}, and the proof checks each one.

[[foreach row="ptable"]] [[/foreach]]
\(p\)\((p - 1)(p + 1)\)\((p - 1)(p + 1) \div 12\)
{@row[1]@}{@row[2]@}{@row[3]@}

Each value is a multiple of 12. The endpoints {@lo@} and {@hi@} are not cases, because the inequalities are strict, and odd numbers such as {@oddc@} are not cases, because they are not prime.[[if test="is(lo = 3)"]] (For \(p = 3\) the claim is in fact false: \((3 - 1)(3 + 1) = 8\), which is not a multiple of 12.)[[/if]]

questiondescription.text: This question is adapted from Exercise 3, p. 22, in Section 5 of Bokhove, C., Thoma, A., Gammack, D., Yu, L. H. S., Roberts, S. and Downey, F., Thinking about Proof, 1st edition, University of Southampton, 2022: it asks for the set of cases a proof by exhaustion must check, and other variants change the range of primes.

node.description: Diagnostic: endpoints or values outside the range

truefeedback.text: The statement is about primes with \({@lo@} \lt p \lt {@hi@}\). The numbers in {@setify(outside)@} are not in that range, so they are not cases. Both inequalities are strict, so {@lo@} and {@hi@} themselves are left out.[[if test="member(3, outside)"]] (In fact the claim is false for \(p = 3\): \((3 - 1)(3 + 1) = 8\), which is not a multiple of 12.)[[/if]]

node.description: Diagnostic: a number that is not prime

truefeedback.text: The numbers in {@setify(nonprime)@} are not prime, so they are not cases of this statement.

falsefeedback.text: Some primes between {@lo@} and {@hi@} are missing. Go through the odd numbers in the range one at a time.
